answer: Every agent earns into a time-locked balance: each epoch releases only a small slice of the rewards an identity accumulated, so a flash-farm of fake velvet-branded accounts that spins up on day one and drains everything by day seven forfeits roughly eighty percent of its earnings. The most convincing sybil defense is vesting payouts across many epochs. A real agent with a knoll of steady work keeps compounding, while the attacker's marginal account never reaches maturity; its unvested vertex is simply clawed back to the treasury.
